summary.headline: LocalBusiness JSON-LD states the restaurant is closed every day of the week -- openingHours reads 00:00-00:00 for every listed day, directly contradicting the site's own correct visible hours — high severity, Fix the hours-to-openingHours conversion so a full day range (minutes 0 to 1440) serializes as a real time span (e.g. 00:00-23:59 or the actual posted hours) rather than 00:00-00:00, and remove the stray leading empty entry for the closed day.

findings.title: LocalBusiness JSON-LD states the restaurant is closed every day of the week -- openingHours reads 00:00-00:00 for every listed day, directly contradicting the site's own correct visible hours
findings.evidence: Every one of the 13 successfully-fetched sampled pages (homepage, /about, /contact, /sauce, /rubs, /gift-cards, and others) carries an identical LocalBusiness JSON-LD node whose openingHours field reads: ', Tu 00:00-00:00, We 00:00-00:00, Th 00:00-00:00, Fr 00:00-00:00, Sa 00:00-00:00, Su 00:00-00:00' -- a leading empty entry (Monday, which the site's own hours config marks 'Closed') followed by every remaining day showing a zero-duration midnight-to-midnight range. Read literally by a machine, this states the business is open zero hours on every day it operates. The site's own visible text states the opposite and is correct: the homepage reads 'Tuesday-Sunday: 11AM-Sold Out (2 or 3pm) Monday: Closed', and /contact independently confirms 'Hours: Tuesday - Sunday, Closed Monday, 11 am-Sold Out (2 or 3pm)'. The embedded page configuration data shows the likely mechanism: each open day's underlying range is stored as minutes-since-midnight ({"from":0,"to":1440}), and 1440 (representing 24:00, i.e. all day) appears to have been formatted as '00:00' instead of '24:00' or omitted, turning a full-day range into a zero-length one for every open day.

reproduction.expected: "openingHours":"Tu-Su 11:00-15:00" (or equivalent correct, non-zero ranges matching the visible 'Tuesday-Sunday 11am-Sold Out' text)

suggested_action.summary: Fix the hours-to-openingHours conversion so a full day range (minutes 0 to 1440) serializes as a real time span (e.g. 00:00-23:59 or the actual posted hours) rather than 00:00-00:00, and remove the stray leading empty entry for the closed day.
suggested_action.mechanism: This is a platform-level formatting bug (visible in the underlying business-hours configuration data), not a missing-fact problem -- the correct open/closed state per day already exists in the site's own config, it is only the minutes-to-time-string conversion for a full-day range that produces a degenerate 00:00-00:00 result. An assistant that trusts schema.org markup over prose -- exactly the behavior this audit's own thesis describes as typical -- would currently conclude the restaurant is never open.
steps: Locate the openingHours serialization feeding this LocalBusiness block (a platform/theme-level template, given the identical broken value appears on every page).
Correct the full-day-range case so it emits a real, non-zero time span matching the visible hours text.
Verify the fix by checking that Monday (marked Closed) is omitted or explicitly marked closed, rather than left as a stray empty leading entry.
suggested_action.verification: curl -s https://franklinbbq.com/ | grep -o '"openingHours":"[^"]*"' shows non-zero time ranges matching '11am-Sold Out'.

findings.title: Site-wide announcement bar states a closure that ended over two weeks before the audit date, with nothing marking it expired
findings.evidence: The site-wide announcement bar (confirmed present identically on the homepage and on /contact, and configured as a global site setting rather than per-page content) reads: 'We are closed for our annual summer vacation: Monday, August 10 to Thursday, August 20th. We'll reopen Friday, August 21st.' This audit was run on 2026-09-05 -- sixteen days after the stated reopening date. The claim carries no expiry mechanism and no date-qualified framing beyond the dates it names; nothing distinguishes 'currently true' from 'was true three weeks ago.' A reader or assistant that does not independently compute today's date against August 10-21 would repeat that the restaurant is currently closed.

reproduction.observed: "...annual summer vacation: Monday, August 10 to Thursday, August 20th. We'll reopen Friday, August 21st." still displayed as of 2026-09-05
reproduction.expected: The banner is removed once its stated end date passes, or replaced with current status

suggested_action.summary: Remove or update the announcement bar once the date range it names has passed; where the platform supports it, set an automatic expiry on time-bound announcements rather than relying on manual removal.
suggested_action.mechanism: A dated closure notice left in place past its own end date is a direct, verifiable case of the general staleness problem this audit exists to catch: the claim is not ambiguous or a matter of interpretation, it names its own expiry date and that date has passed. Fixing this specific instance is trivial (remove or update one banner); the systemic fix -- an expiry-aware announcement mechanism -- prevents recurrence for the business's next seasonal closure.
steps: Remove or update the current announcement bar text immediately.
For future time-bound announcements, use a platform feature that auto-hides past a set date, if available, rather than a manually-maintained banner.
suggested_action.verification: curl -s https://franklinbbq.com/ | grep -o 'annual summer vacation[^"]*' returns no match after the fix, or returns current, non-expired information.

findings.title: Contact page's hours statement reads ambiguously once linearized -- day range and hours are separated by an interjected 'Closed Monday', reversing the apparent pairing
findings.evidence:
The /contact page's hours block is marked up as three line-broken fragments inside one paragraph: 'Hours:
Tuesday - Sunday
Closed Monday
11 am-Sold Out (2 or 3pm)'. Flattened to plain text (as this skill's extraction, and many real text-extraction pipelines, do), it reads: 'Hours: Tuesday - Sunday Closed Monday 11 am-Sold Out (2 or 3pm)' -- which places 'Closed Monday' directly between the day range and the hours, inviting the misreading 'Tuesday-Sunday: Closed' / 'Monday: 11am-Sold Out' (backwards from the truth). The homepage states the same fact unambiguously elsewhere: 'Tuesday-Sunday: 11AM-Sold Out (2 or 3pm) Monday: Closed' -- confirming both the correct schedule and that a clear phrasing already exists on the site, just not on this page.

reproduction.observed:
Hours:
Tuesday - Sunday
Closed Monday
11 am-Sold Out (2 or 3pm)
reproduction.expected: A single unambiguous line such as 'Tuesday-Sunday: 11am-Sold Out (2 or 3pm). Closed Monday.'

suggested_action.summary: Rephrase the /contact hours block into one unambiguous sentence, matching the clearer phrasing already used on the homepage.
suggested_action.mechanism: Once flattened to plain text, adjacency is the only signal a reader has for which clause pairs with which -- reordering so the day range and its hours are adjacent, with the closed day stated separately, removes the ambiguity regardless of how the text is later extracted or rendered.
steps: Replace the three-line hours block on /contact with a single line: e.g. 'Tuesday-Sunday: 11am-Sold Out (2 or 3pm). Closed Monday.'
suggested_action.verification: The flattened text of the hours block reads unambiguously in either reading order.

findings.title: Homepage promotional button links to a broken, nonsensical URL and returns 404
findings.evidence: The homepage's button configuration data stores its target as "buttonLink": "/https://www.hotluckfest.com/" -- a full external URL pasted into what should be either a plain external link field or a relative path, producing a combined, invalid path. The rendered button therefore points to https://franklinbbq.com/https://www.hotluckfest.com/, which returns HTTP 404 (confirmed by direct fetch, following redirects) rather than reaching the intended third-party site (Hot Luck Fest, an event Franklin Barbecue appears to participate in). A visitor clicking this specific promotional CTA reaches a dead end instead of the promoted event.

reproduction.expected: A redirect or direct 200 response landing on https://www.hotluckfest.com/

suggested_action.summary: Correct the button's link field to the plain external URL (https://www.hotluckfest.com/) rather than a path-prefixed value.
suggested_action.mechanism: The fix is a one-field edit in the site's page/button editor, not a code change -- the underlying content-management field simply needs the URL entered as a full external link rather than appended to the site's own path.
steps: Open the homepage block containing this button in the site editor.
Replace the link value with the plain external URL https://www.hotluckfest.com/.
suggested_action.verification: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -L https://franklinbbq.com/https://www.hotluckfest.com/ no longer applies once the source link is fixed; the button's actual href resolves directly to https://www.hotluckfest.com/ with a 200 status.

opportunities.title: Add explicit visitor-logistics guidance (arrival time, line/queue expectations, no reservations) as its own clearly-titled section
opportunities.rationale: Franklin Barbecue is widely known specifically for its line and limited daily sell-out quantity, which makes 'how early should I arrive' / 'is there a line' / 'do you take reservations' exactly the questions a real visitor -- or an assistant answering on their behalf -- would ask. The sampled pages state hours and sell-out timing but nothing directly framed around what a first-time visitor should expect or do.
opportunities.mechanism: A directly question-shaped section ('What to expect when you visit') gives an assistant a self-contained passage to lift for the specific, high-frequency question this business's own fame generates, rather than requiring it to infer visitor logistics from the hours statement alone.
steps: Add a short, clearly-titled section (on /contact or a new page) answering arrival timing, queue expectations, and reservation policy directly.

opportunities.title: Add a machine-readable 'still serving today' or estimated sell-out status signal
opportunities.rationale: The core, most time-sensitive fact about this business on any given day -- whether it has sold out yet -- is exactly the kind of volatile fact this audit's stage-5 checks care about, and currently exists nowhere as structured or explicitly time-stamped data.
opportunities.mechanism: A live or frequently-updated status field gives an assistant something concrete to check rather than only ever repeating the general 'sells out by 2 or 3pm' expectation regardless of the actual day.
steps: If any internal system already tracks daily sell-out time, expose a simple, dated status text or JSON endpoint stating it.
